claim: Root-cause fix (not a workaround) for the boundary-pinning artifact documented in the two superseded nodes above, applied directly to jnwb/onset_fitting.py's caller (scripts/fit_class_onset_latency.py) and rerun on the full 22-session corpus. This is now the current best estimate for the H1/H2/H3 onset-hierarchy test.
root_causes_fixed: causal_exp_smooth needs 5*TAU_SMOOTH_MS=150ms of REAL preceding history to avoid zero-padding its kernel; the original S_WIN_MS/O_WIN_MS gave only 100ms of lookback, so every bin in the analysis window was smoothed against a partially fabricated zero history. Fixed unconditionally: EXTRACTION_MARGIN_MS=150ms is now extracted before the window used for fitting and trimmed off afterward, in fit_one_cell.

S+/S-/omnibus (all p1-aligned) had a baseline window (-100,0ms) sitting inside the region a pre-stimulus ramp could already be elevating -- biasing the fitted baseline upward and pushing apparent onset toward t0=0. Fixed by widening S_WIN_MS to (-500,400)ms and moving S_BASELINE_MS to (-400,-150)ms, using the fx=-500ms fixation-acquisition marker (jnwb.sequence_layout.EPOCH_ONSETS_MS) as a genuine pre-trial reference clear of any plausible ramp onset.

O+/O- baseline window and onset-search semantics were DELIBERATELY NOT changed: the period immediately before an omitted slot is the preceding delay, and an anticipatory omission-expectation ramp toward that slot is the phenomenon O+/O- exist to measure, not noise to be baselined out. Only O_WIN_MS's smoothing-warmup margin was fixed (widened to -250ms start, still safely inside the preceding delay period for all 3 omitted slots, checked against EPOCH_ONSETS_MS).

validation.smoke_test_3_sessions: pinning dropped from ~35-85% to ~9-25% across S+/omnibus before committing to the full rerun

by_class.O+: 4/4 (100%) -- unchanged, by design (baseline window not touched for O classes)
by_class.S-: 0 gate-passing cells at all now (was 5/5 100% pinned before) -- genuinely too sparse to pass the r2 gate once the fit is no longer artificially inflating r2 via a degenerate boundary collapse
by_class.O-: 0 gate-passing cells (was 5/6 83.3% pinned) -- same reasoning as S-

omnibus.note: not significant, but every value is now a real fit (not boundary artifact); V4 (36.5ms) is the only sub-40ms-floor value remaining

S+.note: not significant at p_holm<0.05, but a real, substantially strengthened signal (was rho=0.07 pre-fix). Every area's onset is now above the 40ms minimum-visual-latency floor. This is the class most worth pursuing next (more sessions, or accept the current n=8/p=0.11 as a suggestive-not-confirmed result).

S-.note: genuinely underpowered, not an artifact -- 0 sessions per area now clear the r2 gate

O+.note: unchanged from before the fix; O+ needs more sessions/units, independent of this fix

still_open: S+/omnibus H1/H2/H3 verdicts are not yet significant (p_holm 0.22/0.44) -- the fix removed the artifact, it did not manufacture significance. Whether these become significant with more sessions, or are a genuine null, is unresolved. O+/O-/S- remain unusable for a per-area comparison regardless of this fix -- a data-volume problem, not a method problem.
coordination_note: This fix was applied directly to jnwb/onset_fitting.py's caller (scripts/fit_class_onset_latency.py) in place, since the concurrent Cursor session that originally built this pipeline has ended (per Hamm 2026-08-15) -- no collision risk remains on these files.
